title: Redwood structured output + function-calling demo - Novus Retail
summary: Redwood AE+SE demo of structured output JSON mode and function/tool calling for Novus Retail. Covered JSON schema enforcement, guardrails, streaming structured responses, console walkthrough for per-route schemas, and Dedicated/Private deployment tradeoffs for PII-sensitive checkout logs. Security questions on SOC 2, KMS, audit logs. Agreed next steps: send pricing, security pack, schedule POC benchmark, and provide sample schema + integration guide.
topics: Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private

Priya Singh - Upload security pack (SOC 2 attestation, KMS integration notes, audit log examples) - 2026-05-07
Maya Patel - Provide sample prompt set and success criteria for checkout extraction POC - 2026-05-10

meeting_header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood Solutions), Maya Patel (Novus Head of ML), Ethan Gray (Platform Eng), Samir Kahn (SecOps), Lily Park (PM)
transcript:
[00:00] Alice Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alice from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Diego is our SE and Priya is joining for the console walkthrough. Quick intros?
[00:15] Maya Patel: Hi yeah Maya here, Head of ML at Novus Retail. We're focused on product search and checkout NLP, interested in structured extraction and integrations with our pricing engine.
[00:30] Ethan Gray: Ethan, platform eng, I'll be evaluating deployment and network stuff, VPCs, firewalls.
[00:40] Samir Kahn: Samir SecOps, security and compliance questions.
[00:50] Alice Chen: Great, agenda for today is structured output JSON mode, schema enforcement and tool/function calling flows, then console demo, then q&a. We'll try to keep it tight.
[01:10] Diego Ramos: Cool I can start with an example. So imagine we want a JSON payload for checkout extraction: items, sku, price_cents, quantity, discount_applied boolean, and a nested shipping object. In Redwood's structured output mode we can provide a JSON schema and the model will emit JSON that follows the schema.
[01:35] Lily Park: Sorry, nested objects are okay? Our product has variable attributes per item.
[01:42] Diego Ramos: Yes, arrays and nested objects are supported in the schema. We also have per-route schemas in the Console so you can pin strict vs permissive parsing.
[02:00] Maya Patel: How strict is "strict"? We worry about hallucinated fields or missing fields breaking downstream.
[02:10] Diego Ramos: Good question. We have a validation layer \u2014 you can choose hard rejection (model output that doesn't pass schema is discarded and we return an error) or auto-repair mode where we attempt to coerce types or fill defaults. We surface confidence and parsing warnings to the response metadata.
[02:35] Ethan Gray: What about latency when you enforce these checks?
[02:40] Diego Ramos: Minimal overhead \u2014 the schema validator runs client-side in our runtime, typically a few milliseconds. The bigger latency factors are model choice, input length, and batching. If you run hosted small models it'll be faster; dedicated capacity gives you predictable p99s.
[02:58] Alice Chen: Also note we have streaming structured output \u2014 the model can stream partial JSON chunks which is helpful for long payloads.
[03:10] Samir Kahn: On security, does that streaming expose partial PII to logs? We need to know retention and redaction points.
[03:20] Priya Singh: Good point. In Private/Dedicated modes you control log retention and can enable automatic redaction rules. Our hosted API has retention defaults but we offer enterprise options and KMS-backed encryption for payloads at rest.
[03:40] Samir Kahn: SOC 2? SSO?
[03:42] Priya Singh: Yes SOC 2 Type II available; we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and integrations with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments. We'll share the security pack after the call.
[04:00] Maya Patel: Can you show the function-calling flow? We want to call our price-check service and also have the model call a resolver that hits internal APIs.
[04:12] Diego Ramos: Sure. We demo a function call where the model returns a structured "call_tool" object with name and args that match your tool schema. Redwood can then automatically invoke your tool (server-side) or let you handle the call client-side. I'll demo the auto-invoke flow.
[04:35] [screen share starts] Diego Ramos: Here's a prompt with a schema and a "tools" definition. The model suggests calling "price_lookup" with sku="ABC123" and region="us-east-1". We validate args against the tool's JSON schema before invoking.
[05:00] Lily Park: If the model suggests a malformed arg, does Redwood block it?
[05:05] Diego Ramos: Yes we validate; by default we reject malformed calls and log them. You can set a permissive mode to auto-coerce minor mismatches but it's off by default for safety.
[05:18] Ethan Gray: Do we have sample latency numbers for function calls that hit an internal service? Say an internal price lookup that's 50ms?
[05:25] Diego Ramos: Total end-to-end depends on model generation + validation + invocation. For a fast internal call (50ms) + a 30ms model token stretch you might see ~120-200ms depending on routing. With Dedicated capacity you get tighter variance; hosted is subject to multi-tenant noise.
[05:45] Maya Patel: We're concerned about cost too \u2014 calling a model for every checkout might be expensive. Thoughts on batching or caching?
[05:55] Diego Ramos: We recommend prefix KV cache for repeated context (customer id, common SKUs) and request-level caching for deterministic responses. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching windows and TTLs; we also support local function invocation for cheap deterministic lookups and only call model for complex extraction.
[06:20] [00:06:20] Alice Chen: Quick qualification: what volume are we talking?
[06:25] Maya Patel: Peak 2000 checkouts/minute during promotions, average 300/min.
[06:32] Diego Ramos: For that, Dedicated with autoscaling pools is a common pattern. We'll size GPUs based on your tokens per request and p99 latency targets.
[06:45] Lily Park: Do you support quantized models? We run custom quantized variants for cost.
[06:50] Diego Ramos: Yes, runtime supports 4-bit and 8-bit quantized models and we have recommendations per workload. There are quality tradeoffs; Optimize can run a quick eval against your prompt set.
[07:10] Samir Kahn: On compliance, can audit logs be forwarded to our SIEM?
[07:14] Priya Singh: Yes we can stream audit logs to your cloud account or SIEM; in Private deployments you can keep logs entirely inside your VPC.
[07:25] Ethan Gray: Network details \u2014 VPC peering vs PrivateLink?
[07:29] Priya Singh: We support both depending on cloud provider. For on-prem we have an on-prem package.
[07:38] [screen share: Console] Diego Ramos: In the Console here you can create a route, attach a JSON schema, pick model family, and set policy: strict vs permissive, fallback model, and streaming on/off. You can also set per-route cost limits and tracing.
[08:00] Diego Ramos: I'll demo a canary rollout \u2014 we have a traffic split. You can also configure automatic fallback to a cheaper model if latency spikes or errors exceed threshold.
[08:20] Maya Patel: If the model fails schema in strict mode, what's the UX?
[08:24] Diego Ramos: The call returns a 422 with the parsing error and a structured debug object showing the raw model output, parsed attempts, and confidence scores.
[08:38] Lily Park: Can we get example logs?
[08:40] Priya Singh: We'll include sample audit logs in the security pack.
[08:44] [09:00] Alice Chen: Quick demo of the guardrails \u2014 we can attach a policy to block out-of-scope tool names, rate-limit tool invocations, and require explicit allow-lists for internal endpoints.
[09:20] Diego Ramos: Here's an example where the schema requires price_cents as integer. The model emitted "$12.99" in one run; auto-repair coerced to 1299 and flagged a warning. In strict mode that would have failed.
[09:45] Samir Kahn: That coercion worries me; we'd prefer strict for money fields.
[09:50] Diego Ramos: Totally understood \u2014 money fields are a common strict setting.
[09:58] Maya Patel: How do we integrate the tool calls with our auth? We use short-lived tokens via our internal STS.
[10:05] Diego Ramos: We support injecting ephemeral creds at invocation time; or you can proxy calls through your gateway. For auto-invoke we provide a webhook call that includes signed metadata; you can enforce mTLS or token exchange.
[10:22] Lily Park: Any examples of error handling patterns?
[10:26] Diego Ramos: Yes, we recommend idempotent tool calls with retries and use the model's generated confidence to decide human-in-the-loop. The Console has retry policies for tool invocation failures.
[10:40] [11:00] Maya Patel: For the POC we want to run 1k synthetic checkouts and compare structured extraction accuracy and latency for hosted vs dedicated.
[11:08] Alice Chen: Perfect. We'll run a benchmark guide and provide suggested cluster sizes.
[11:14] Ethan Gray: Network test \u2014 can you run a latency run from us-east-1 to your hosted region?
[11:18] Diego Ramos: We'll include a perf script for that.
[11:23] Samir Kahn: One more on data: can we disable retention per-route?
[11:26] Priya Singh: Yes, retention can be configured per-route. Private mode gives you full control.
[11:34] [11:35] Diego Ramos: Demo wrap-up \u2014 showed schema enforcement, auto-repair vs strict, function calling with validation, and Console policies for fallback and canaries.
[11:45] Alice Chen: Any final questions?
[11:48] Maya Patel: Two quick ones: 1) can we see sample code for the function-calling client? 2) what's the cost delta rough for Dedicated vs hosted for our volume?
[11:58] Diego Ramos: We'll share a sample client lib in multiple langs; cost delta depends on tokens and reserved commit, but Dedicated usually lowers unit cost at volume. I'll give ballpark numbers in the follow-up.
[12:12] Lily Park: Also request for a sample schema repo so our devs can iterate.
[12:18] Alice Chen: We'll send sample schemas and a starter repo.
[12:25] [12:25] Alice Chen: Recap and next steps: Redwood sends pricing, security pack, sample schema repo, benchmark guide. Novus to share prompt set and success criteria. Schedule POC kick-off for next week.
[12:40] Maya Patel: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[12:44] Samir Kahn: Thanks.
[12:46] Alice Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the docs.
[12:50] [call ends]
